papers.title: BTBD9-driven IMPDH2 ubiquitination governs sleep homeostasis by gating adenosine metabolism in the basal forebrain.
papers.summary: Identified a BTBD9-IMPDH2-adenosine pathway in which CRL3(BTBD9)-mediated ubiquitination of IMPDH2 at K195 relieves GTP-dependent allosteric inhibition, limiting adenosine accumulation and sleep pressure in the mouse basal forebrain. Basal forebrain Btbd9 deletion increased NREM sleep and extracellular adenosine, whereas AAV-delivered interfering peptides targeting the BTBD9-IMPDH2 interaction rescued BTBD9 overexpression-induced abnormal wakefulness.

papers.title: Distinct whole-brain c-Fos expression mapping following acute and chronic partial sleep deprivation in mice.
papers.summary: Used HD-fMOST whole-brain c-Fos mapping to compare neuronal activation after acute sleep deprivation (ASD), recovery sleep, and two weeks of chronic partial sleep deprivation (CPSD) in mice. ASD broadly upregulated c-Fos that was largely restored by 2 h recovery sleep, whereas CPSD predominantly suppressed c-Fos with complex regional disparities and distinct network-level activation patterns.

papers.title: Closed-Loop Acoustic Stimulation of Slow Oscillations Using a Wireless EEG Headband: A Polysomnography-Validated Feasibility Study.
papers.summary: Tested a real-time modeling-based closed-loop acoustic stimulation approach using a wireless forehead EEG headband in healthy participants during one night, with simultaneous PSG as reference. SO phase was targeted near the intended phase, and stimulation immediately enhanced SO dynamics plus sustained increases in SO density and delta/SO power (0.75-5 Hz) in both headband and PSG signals.

papers.title: Sleep and Drowsiness in Cattle: A Narrative Review of Physiology, Measurement, and Methodological Challenges.
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: Narrative review of 22 primary studies synthesizing cattle NREM/REM sleep and drowsing physiology, measurement approaches (PSG, behavior, accelerometry, automated classification), and methodological limitations. Reported sleep and drowsing durations vary widely, drowsing overlaps with quiet wakefulness and light sleep, and evidence remains insufficient to establish causal links between sleep variation and cattle health, welfare, or performance.

papers.title: A Unified Flexible Large Polysomnography Model for Sleep Staging and Downstream Clinical Screening
papers.summary: Presents LPSGM, a large polysomnography model trained on 220,500 hours from 16 public datasets using domain-adaptive pretraining and flexible channel configurations. It achieved expert-level sleep staging (kappa 0.845 vs inter-expert 0.850) and supported downstream screening of narcolepsy (84.2% accuracy), severe OSA (AUC 0.874), and depression (AUC 0.801, cross-dataset 0.965).

papers.title: Sleep-dependent DNA methylation remodeling in basolateral amygdala fear engrams.
papers.summary: Using activity-dependent tagging with methylome and transcriptome sequencing of basolateral amygdala engram neurons after contextual fear conditioning, the authors show fear learning drives coordinated CpG and CpH DNA methylation remodeling specifically in engrams, with CpH methylation as a distinct epigenetic component; post-learning sleep deprivation partially reversed these changes and impaired recall. Multi-omic integration identified Mid1 as a learning- and sleep-regulated methylation target whose BLA-wide and engram-specific knockdown impaired fear memory consolidation.

papers.title: A Physiology-Informed Deep Learning Approach for Sleep-EEG Brain Age Estimation.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: Developed a physiology-informed deep learning framework estimating brain age from whole-night PSG across ~10,000 recordings (MAE 5.89 years; external validation MAE 5.41 years), with a trainable Gabor filter bank providing explicit spectral readouts. Each 10-year increase in brain age gap was associated with 19% higher all-cause and 25% higher cardiovascular mortality risk, and SHAP analysis revealed age-dependent spectral shifts and sleep-stage changes.

papers.title: The role of BDNF, CREB, DAT, GFAP and Arc in manic- and OCD-like behavioral phenotypes in both sexes of rats exposed to REM sleep deprivation.
papers.summary: Examined behavioral and hippocampal molecular effects of 14 days of REM sleep deprivation in male and female rats, finding hyperlocomotion, decreased anxiety, and increased OCD-like and stereotyped behaviors alongside decreased BDNF, CREB, DAT, and Arc and increased GFAP expression, with more pronounced effects in females except for anxiety-like behavior and CREB.

papers.title: RefineSleepNet: Task-Driven Signal-Domain Transformation for EEG/EOG Sleep Staging.
papers.summary: Proposes RefineSleepNet, a sequence-to-sequence framework that separates task-driven signal refinement of EEG/EOG waveforms (SRU-Net) from epoch feature extraction, followed by fused sequence attention. In subject-independent 10-fold cross-validation it reached accuracy/macro-F1 of 84.5%/79.8% (Sleep-EDF-39), 83.5%/78.1% (Sleep-EDF-153), and 80.3%/78.1% (ISRUC-3).

papers.title: CSPT-SleepNet: An Automatic Sleep Staging Framework Integrating Center-Driven Sequence Supervision and Multimodal Pyramid Token Encoding.
papers.summary: Proposes CSPT-SleepNet, integrating center-driven sequence supervision with multimodal pyramid token encoding for EEG/EOG/EMG sleep staging. Subject-independent cross-validation yielded accuracy/macro-F1 of 87.93%/83.53% (Sleep-EDF-20), 85.81%/80.87% (Sleep-EDF-78), and 84.06%/82.86% (ISRUC-S3), with N1 recognition remaining challenging.

papers.title: Daylight exposure improves sleep and subsequent sleepiness
papers.summary: In a randomized crossover study of 10 healthy adults, afternoon high-intensity daylight versus attenuated-light outdoor walks did not shift circadian phase but produced faster accumulation of nighttime delta power, greater NREM sleep, less wakefulness after sleep onset, and reduced next-morning sleepiness.

papers.title: Postpartum mice display distinct behavioral and neuroimmune responses to chronic circadian disruption.
papers.summary: Tested whether postpartum mice show greater behavioral and neuroimmune sensitivity to chronic phase advancement (6-h phase advance every 4 days, P0-18) than nulliparous controls. Chronic circadian disruption produced parity-dependent increases in grooming and reduced nest preference, reduced medial preoptic area microglia density in parous females, and parity × CPA interaction effects on synapse organization and RNA processing transcripts.

papers.title: MM-Net: A Multimodal Multi-Task Network for Sleep Staging and Sleep Apnea Assessment After Ischemic Stroke
papers.summary: MM-Net is a multimodal multi-task framework combining sleep-adapted EEG-EOG representations with cardiorespiratory features via cross-attention and ridge-based embedding alignment to jointly perform sleep staging and respiratory-event detection after ischemic stroke. On iSLEEPS it reached 76.3% staging accuracy (κ=0.656) and 0.825 respiratory-event AUC, and embedding alignment improved staging by 1.4 percentage points over a frozen encoder (p=0.020).

papers.title: Ketones and Sleep: A Narrative Review of Mechanisms, Preclinical Models, and Human Evidence.
papers.summary: Narrative review synthesizing mechanistic, preclinical, and human evidence on ketone bodies and sleep. It reports that AcAc (but not BHB) increases NREM slow-wave activity and suppresses glutamate release in mice, while human findings are suggestive but heterogeneous, with ketone effects on sleep conditional rather than universally sleep-promoting.

papers.title: Indirect Skin Homeostasis Modulation by an Essential Oil Blend in Mice with Insomnia Comorbid Anxiety: Sensitivity of Dermal Fibroblasts to Exogenously Applied Circulating Molecules.
papers.summary: In a para-chlorophenylalanine-induced mouse model of insomnia comorbid anxiety, an essential oil blend (300 mg/kg intraperitoneal) alleviated anxiety- and insomnia-like behaviors, normalized brain neurotransmitters and hormones, and altered serum/skin cortisol, melatonin, 5-hydroxytryptamine, IL-10, and type I collagen; cultured dermal fibroblasts showed molecule-specific responses in oxidative stress, inflammation, and extracellular matrix synthesis. The authors caution that the in vitro assays show cellular sensitivity only and do not establish a causal brain-skin axis mechanism.

papers.title: Effects of Circadian Phase and Exercise Training on Systemic and Tissue-Specific Redox Responses in Mice Fed a High-Fat Diet.
papers.summary: In high-fat-diet-fed male C57BL/6J mice, 8 weeks of treadmill training at ZT3 versus ZT15 was compared for systemic and tissue-specific redox responses; exercise increased plasma biological antioxidant potential irrespective of phase, while tissue redox-related transcriptional changes (e.g., soleus Hmox1, hepatic Keap1) were mainly circadian-phase-dependent and tissue-specific. The authors note that whether active-phase exercise confers a redox advantage requires further investigation.

papers.title: Computational approaches to deep learning-driven EEG analysis for neurological disease diagnosis: a systematic review.
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes deep learning computational approaches for EEG-based diagnosis of neurological diseases, covering architectures such as CNNs, RNNs, hybrid models, GANs, autoencoders, LLMs, and transformers across epilepsy, Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and related disorders. It also discusses preprocessing and denoising strategies and identifies limited data, interpretability, inter-subject variability, and clinical translation as key challenges.

papers.title: Algorithmic loops and the developing brain: a narrative review of dopaminergic mechanisms, sleep disruption, and neuroplasticity.
papers.summary: This narrative review proposes a mechanistic framework in which chronic exposure to algorithmically optimized short-form looping video may drive homeostatic striatal D2/D3 receptor downregulation and attentional dysregulation, amplified by disruption of slow-wave sleep and glymphatic clearance. It cites ABCD cohort associations with grey matter volume, reward-circuit activation, and executive function, and proposes a cross-species multimodal longitudinal research program including primate digital self-administration and human polysomnography.

papers.title: A transient decrease in night-to-night variability of REM sleep before myocardial infarction
papers.summary: In a matched cohort from the All of Us Research Program (45 first-MI cases, 450 controls) using Fitbit sleep data, night-to-night variability of REM-sleep fraction showed a transient pattern before MI, decreasing at days 30-16 and returning toward baseline over days 15-1 (max-T p<0.001). The SD decrease was not seen before pneumonia, fracture/appendicitis, or all-cause admissions, and person-specific scoring discriminated cases from controls with AUCs up to 0.66.

papers.title: Tablet-Camera Iris Landmarks and EEG/PPG-Derived Arousal Indices During Naturalistic Reading: Geometric Confounding and Exploratory Within-Subject Associations.
papers.summary: Evaluated whether MediaPipe iris landmark distances from a tablet camera estimate EEG/PPG-derived arousal during naturalistic reading across 43,923 thirty-second windows from 48 participants; raw iris distances correlated weakly with EEG alpha but face scale explained 93% of their variance, and after full adjustment for ocular luminance and head pose the alpha association was nonsignificant (r=+0.021).

papers.title: SOCS3 Suppression Is Associated with Hippocampal Inflammation in a Mouse Model of Intermittent Hypoxia.
papers.summary: In a mouse intermittent hypoxia model and BV2 cells, IH was associated with impaired water maze performance, reduced hippocampal SOCS3, and elevated inflammatory markers, MALAT1, and H3K27me3; SOCS3 overexpression reduced TRAF6, NF-κB p65, TNF-α, and IL-1β, while MALAT1 knockdown increased SOCS3.

papers.title: Interventional Effects and Neurometabolic Regulation of a Panax quinquefolius-Containing Herbal Extract (JYF) in Diazepam Withdrawal Syndrome in Mice.
papers.summary: Characterized a Panax quinquefolius-containing herbal extract (JYF) and tested it in a diazepam-withdrawal mouse model, finding that JYF attenuated withdrawal-associated weight loss, anxiety-like behavior, sleep fragmentation, and abnormal EEG activity, with metabolomic shifts in tryptophan and phenylalanine pathways and monoamine neurotransmitters moving toward control levels.

papers.title: Association of Total Atherosclerosis Burden of Baroreceptor-Resident Arteries with Heart Rate Variability and Its Circadian Rhythm in Patients with Ischemic Stroke.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 253 first-ever ischemic stroke patients, higher CTA-assessed total atherosclerosis burden of baroreceptor-resident arteries was nonlinearly associated with lower 24 h SDNN (1.67 ms decrease per 1-point increase) and reduced circadian SDNN amplitude in intermediate- and high-burden tertiles.

papers.title: Editorial: Supporting the mental health of neurodivergent adults through sleep and circadian based interventions.
papers.summary: This editorial outlines the challenge of sleep and circadian disruptions affecting mental health in autistic, ADHD, and AuDHD adults and proposes a basic science research program to inform scalable interventions. It emphasizes co-design and longitudinal combination of objective and subjective sleep/circadian measures with mental health symptom data, highlighting the sleep/circadian profiles of AuDHD individuals as a critical gap.

papers.title: Using High-Performance Liquid Chromatography to Study Alterations in Biogenic Amines in Drosophila Models of Brain Disorders.
papers.summary: This protocol describes HPLC coupled with electrochemical detection for simultaneous quantification of dopamine, serotonin, and octopamine in Drosophila brain tissue, addressing the technical challenge of low nanomolar-to-femtomolar biogenic amine levels. Applied to an alpha-synuclein Parkinson's disease fly model, it revealed significantly elevated dopamine with unchanged serotonin relative to controls, consistent with early compensatory dopaminergic mechanisms.

papers.title: Normative Deviation Modeling for EEG-based Depression Detection
papers.summary: Proposes normative deviation modeling for EEG-based major depressive disorder detection, training structural and distributional healthy-control reference models and integrating their deviations at scalar (S-NDD) or feature (F-NDD) level, with target HC-assisted score calibration for cross-source evaluation. On two public EEG datasets, the normative deviation-guided approaches were effective under subject-independent within-source and bidirectional cross-source settings.

papers.title: Age-Adjusted Exploratory Analysis of Spectral, Aperiodic, and Microstate EEG Features in Multiple Sclerosis.
papers.summary: Age-adjusted exploratory analysis of resting-state EEG in the BrainLat dataset found significant MS-versus-control differences in global bandwidth, global aperiodic offset, and offset at all 128 channels, while spectral, exponent, PSD, and microstate measures did not survive FDR correction; non-overlapping age ranges limit interpretation.

papers.title: Theta-band EEG changes following sequential rTMS and tACS in fibromyalgia: A randomized controlled pilot study
papers.summary: In an exploratory randomized controlled pilot study of 10 adults with fibromyalgia, sequential 10-Hz rTMS over left primary motor cortex followed by 10 daily bilateral 10-Hz tACS increased resting-state theta power in the active group but not controls (Time x Group F(1,8)=8.70, p=.018), with larger increases posteriorly. No significant interaction effects were found for delta, alpha, or beta power.

papers.title: Ozone as a Catalyst for Alzheimer's Disease and Sleep Disorders: Implications for Neurodegeneration Induced by Air Pollution.
papers.summary: Narrative review synthesizing experimental and epidemiological evidence that tropospheric ozone generates a systemic oxidative-inflammatory signal affecting the CNS, with sleep/circadian disruption and Alzheimer's-related pathology as potentially reinforcing downstream outcomes; concludes ozone is a biologically plausible but not yet epidemiologically confirmed risk factor.

papers.title: Oxidative Stress in Pediatric Obstructive Sleep Apnea Syndrome: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: Narrative review summarizing mechanisms, biomarkers, and clinical consequences of oxidative stress in pediatric obstructive sleep apnea syndrome, including intermittent hypoxia-driven redox pathways (NADPH oxidases, HIF-1α, NF-κB, mitochondrial dysfunction, ER stress) and associated endothelial, cardiovascular, neurocognitive, and metabolic injury. It reports that oxidative and end-organ injury do not consistently parallel the apnea-hypopnea index and that methodological heterogeneity and lack of standardized pediatric reference values limit biomarker use.

papers.title: Overt and Covert Speech-State Classification from Tripolar Concentric Ring Electrode EEG: A 4 mm and 10 mm Configuration Study.
papers.summary: Applied 4 mm and 10 mm tripolar concentric ring electrodes to record EEG during 200 picture-naming trials (100 overt, 100 covert) in 16 participants, comparing classification with LDA, SVM, and EEGNet. Overt speech produced higher task-to-baseline ratios than covert speech, and EEGNet achieved the highest mean accuracy (84.06±15.57%), followed by SVM (81.56±14.23%) and LDA (76.56±15.30%).

papers.title: Total polyphenols from Hemerocallis citrina Baroni leaves improve sleep quality in mice with perimenopausal insomnia and are associated with altered expression of 5-HT1AR, ADCY5, PKA, and GABRA2.
papers.summary: Evaluated total polyphenols from Hemerocallis citrina Baroni leaves (HLTP) in a VCD+PCPA mouse model of perimenopausal insomnia using behavioral, EEG/EMG polysomnography, biochemical, Western blot, and multi-omics analyses. High-dose HLTP shortened NREM/REM sleep latencies, prolonged NREM bout duration, increased NREM sleep time, and altered 5-HT1AR, GABRA2, ADCY5, and PKA expression, with exploratory gut microbiota, serum metabolomic, and brain transcriptomic changes.

papers.title: Strategies to establish a biologically defined Parkinson's disease cohort prior to the onset of clinically significant motor symptoms
papers.summary: The Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative describes recruitment strategies to enroll individuals before clinically significant motor symptoms via polysomnogram-confirmed REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD) and central hyposmia testing, showing all strategies enriched for CSF alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay positivity. RBD+Hyposmia (94%) and Hyposmia+DEB (85%) were more likely CSF aSynSAA+ than RBD-Hyposmia (40%) and Hyposmia-DEB (55%), and CSF aSynSAA+ individuals showed heterogeneity in mood, autonomic, and cognitive symptoms.

papers.title: Molecular mechanisms of YZG-331 ameliorated insomnia based on the gut microbiota-drug interaction.
papers.summary: Investigated how gut microbiota contribute to the anti-insomnia efficacy and metabolism of YZG-331, showing it regulates microbial tryptophan metabolism and 5-HT production, increases Lactobacillus and Muribaculaceae abundance with Lactobacillus reuteri as a key species, activates the BH4 cofactor system to promote TPH activity, and raises intestinal butyric acid levels. The study provides the first evidence for the gut microbiota's role in YZG-331's therapeutic mechanism and metabolic processing in insomnia.

papers.title: Sleep Disturbances and Circadian Phase Delay in People Living with Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV): A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 15 studies found a high prevalence of poor sleep quality and delayed circadian phase in people living with HIV, with these chronobiological alterations linked to systemic inflammation, altered melatonin levels, impaired cognition, and metabolic changes involving leptin, ghrelin, adiponectin, and PPAR signaling. The authors noted an absence of clinical trials and proposed chronotherapeutic interventions plus sleep hygiene as complements to antiretroviral therapy.

papers.title: Menopausal Symptom Burden and Self-Reported Poor Sleep Quality Among Japanese Working Women Aged 40 Years and Older: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.summary: Exploratory cross-sectional study of 79 Japanese working women aged 40 and older combining Simplified Menopausal Index scores, self-reported sleep quality, and wearable EEG-measured sleep duration. After adjusting for age and objective sleep duration, total and domain-specific menopausal symptom burden were associated with self-reported poor sleep quality, and associations persisted in sensitivity analyses excluding the sleep-related SMI item.

papers.title: Exploratory Metabolomic and Metagenomic Profiling of Fecal Samples in Isolated REM Sleep Behavior Disorder.
papers.summary: In an exploratory cross-sectional multi-omics study of fecal samples from 21 isolated REM sleep behavior disorder patients and 15 controls, branched-chain fatty acids were selectively increased, volatile indole reduced, and the microbiome depleted of Blautia and Faecalibacterium; integrated host-microbe signatures discriminated patients from controls with 84.8% cross-validated accuracy.

papers.title: Sleep quality, circadian rhythm disruption, functioning, and treatment adherence in major depression: a cross-sectional exploratory study.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional exploratory study of 110 outpatients with major depression examining sleep quality (PSQI), biological rhythm disruption (BRIAN), functioning, medication adherence, and depression severity. Poorer sleep quality correlated with lower social functioning and adherence and with greater circadian disruption and depression severity, and in regression biological rhythm disruption was the only independent predictor of sleep quality (beta = 0.445, R-squared = 0.429).

papers.title: Seasonal Variation, Circadian Patterns, and Night Eating Syndrome Among Older Adults: The Mediating Role of Sleep Quality.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional path analysis of 336 community-dwelling older adults, sleep quality significantly mediated the associations of seasonal variation with circadian pattern (41% of the modeled association) and with night eating syndrome (37%), with 85.1% reporting poor sleep quality and 23.2% meeting criteria for full night eating syndrome.

papers.title: Depressive Symptoms, Insomnia-Related Difficulties and Self-Rated Health Among Community-Dwelling Adults Aged 40 Years and Older in Western China: A Cross-Sectional Structural Equation Modelling Study.
papers.summary: Structural equation modelling in 433 community-dwelling adults aged ≥40 in western China found an insomnia-derived construct had the largest direct association with self-rated health (β=0.383) and statistically mediated an indirect association between depressive symptoms and self-rated health (0.208).

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
